title: Determine if assets/sync-opencode-copilot-profiles.sh can be removed
description:
So assets/sync-opencode-copilot-profiles.sh regenerates the static Copilot profile from the main OpenCode config, keeping selected hand-authored agent entries and mapping OpenAI-backed agents to GitHub Copilot equivalents.
   That said, after the new runtime merge work, there is some overlap:
   - sync-opencode-copilot-profiles.sh creates/updates the checked-in profiles/copilot/opencode.jsonc.
   - opencode-sync-workspace-overrides.sh also remaps OpenAI models at runtime when copilot is active.
   So the Copilot profile generator is partly historical and partly useful as a checked-in/fallback artifact. The runtime helper is now the main thing that makes stacked profiles work.
   My honest take: the current behavior is correct, but the naming/flow is confusing. A future cleanup could either:
   1. keep the Copilot generator but document it as “derive checked-in Copilot profile from base config”, or
   2. remove most of the generated Copilot profile and rely fully on runtime remapping.
   I would not remove it casually in this change because it may still serve as fallback/static profile behavior, but it is a reasonable simplification target.

title: Expansion of Renovate to repos in personal-dotfiles GitLab project
devcontainer-launch.sh to show list of devcontainers & update iTerm profile automatically
description:
Mr. Dutt, yes, this option exists, with one caveat: the menu selection is easy; making iTerm choose a profile via Automatic Profile Switching depends on what iTerm can detect after the container shell starts.
   Best options:
   1. Launcher-driven menu
      - Add something like:
         devcontainer-launch --menu
      
      or make no-args interactive.
      - It reads configs/devcontainer-sync.jsonc.
      - Shows devcontainers via fzf if available, otherwise a basic numbered shell menu.
      - Launches the selected container.
   2. iTerm profile switching
      There are two ways:
      A. More reliable: launcher emits iTerm profile switch escape
      - Manifest could define:
         "iterm_profile": "Homelab IaC Devcontainer"
      
      - Launcher emits an iTerm escape sequence before entering the container.
      - This is deterministic and directly tied to your menu selection.
      - This is not technically “Automatic Profile Switching,” but it achieves the same outcome more reliably.
      B. True iTerm Automatic Profile Switching
      - Possible if the container shell has iTerm shell integration and exposes stable metadata.
      - iTerm can switch based on things like user/host/path.
      - We would need a stable container hostname/path rule, for example:
      - container hostname: homelab-iac-devcontainer
      - working directory: /workspaces/homelab-IaC
      - This may require devcontainer config changes, and it is more brittle.
   My recommendation: defer this, but when we do it, implement:
   devcontainer-launch --menu
   plus optional manifest fields like:
   "terminal": {
   "iterm_profile": "Homelab IaC Devcontainer"
   }
   Then the launcher can switch iTerm explicitly before launching the selected devcontainer. 
   That’s cleaner than trying to force Automatic Profile Switching to infer the right profile indirectly.
notes: While this feature in isolation might be theoretically possible, using the dev containers directly in iTerm via devcontainer-launch.sh is proving to be not as effective as I'd hoped. The browser integration for opencode-plannotator does not work in this approach so I'm not sure how much value there is implementing this feature.
